::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[On the equality of derivatives of two functions.](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1946472/on-the-equality-of-derivatives-of-two-functions), asked by [Q_p](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/704680/q-p) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-09-29; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Let $f$ and $g$ be two differentiable functions of $x$. Suppose that
>
> $$\dfrac{d^{n}f}{dx^n} = \dfrac{d^{n}g}{dx^n}$$ for some positive real $n$, where the derivatives are evaluated at $x=\alpha$.
>
> Does this necessarily mean that $f(\alpha) = g(\alpha)$ ?.
:::

For *some* $n$?  Not even close.  Let $n=1$, $f(x) =x$, and $g(x)=x+1$.  Then $f'(x) = g'(x)$, but $f(\alpha) \neq g(\alpha)$, not at any point $\alpha$.
